query: OpenAI-compatible API required endpoints model list connection
raw_response:
### Model Connectivity Check with cURL

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/reference/monitoring

This command checks if Open WebUI can reach your model providers and list available models. It requires an API key for authentication.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  http://your-open-webui-instance:8080/api/models
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Open WebUI Connection to llama.cpp

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/alternatives/llama-cpp

Add the llama.cpp server's OpenAI-compatible API endpoint to Open WebUI's connection settings. This allows Open WebUI to access models served by llama.cpp.

```text
# In Admin → Settings → Connections, add:
# URL: http://localhost:8081/v1
```

--------------------------------

### Configure OpenClaw API Endpoint

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/connect-an-agent/openclaw

Enable the OpenAI-compatible API endpoint in your OpenClaw configuration file by setting `enabled` to `true` for `chatCompletions`. Restart the gateway for changes to apply.

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "http": {
      "endpoints": {
        "chatCompletions": {
          "enabled": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Connect Gemini via Google AI API in Open WebUI

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/alternatives/gemini

To use Gemini models in Open WebUI, obtain an API key from Google AI Studio. Then, configure a new connection in Open WebUI's Admin settings with the specified base URL and your API key. Gemini models will then be available in the model selector.

```bash
https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Connection Timeout for Model List

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/connect-a-provider/starting-with-openai

Increase the timeout for fetching the model list if your API provider is slow to respond. The default is 10 seconds.

```bash
# Increase timeout for slow networks (default is 10 seconds)
AIOHTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MODEL_LIST=15
```

--------------------------------

### Generate Responses via OpenAI-Compatible API

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/reference/api-endpoints

Uses the OpenAI-compatible responses endpoint proxied through the Ollama router.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/ollama/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "llama3.2",
  "input": "Why is the sky blue?"
}'
```

--------------------------------

### Generate Embeddings via OpenAI-Compatible API

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/reference/api-endpoints

Uses the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint proxied through the Ollama router.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/ollama/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "llama3.2",
  "input": "Open WebUI is great!"
}'
```

--------------------------------

### Additional Endpoints

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/features/chat-conversations/audio/text-to-speech/openai-edge-tts-integration

Lists available endpoints for retrieving TTS models and voices.

```APIDOC
## Additional Endpoints

- **POST/GET /v1/models**: Lists available TTS models.
- **POST/GET /v1/voices**: Lists `edge-tts` voices for a given language / locale.
- **POST/GET /v1/voices/all**: Lists all `edge-tts` voices, with language support information.

_Note: The `/v1` prefix is optional. These endpoints can be disabled by setting the environment variable `EXPAND_API=False`._
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Model List Fetch Timeout

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/troubleshooting/connection-error

Set a lower timeout value to prevent the UI from hanging when attempting to connect to unreachable API endpoints.

```bash
# Set a shorter timeout (in seconds) for faster failure on unreachable endpoints
AIOHTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MODEL_LIST=3
```

--------------------------------

### Configure OpenAI API passthrough

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/advanced-topics/hardening

Controls the proxy endpoint for forwarding requests to upstream OpenAI-compatible APIs.

```bash
ENABLE_OPENAI_API_PASSTHROUGH=false
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Model Caching via Environment Variables

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/troubleshooting/performance

Enable base model list caching and set the TTL for external API responses to improve responsiveness.

```bash
ENABLE_BASE_MODELS_CACHE=True
```

```bash
MODELS_CACHE_TTL=300
```

--------------------------------

### Model Management Endpoints

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/reference/api-endpoints

Endpoints for programmatic management of custom models including export, import, sync, create, update, and delete operations.

```APIDOC
## GET /api/v1/models/export

### Description
Export all custom models as a JSON array.

## POST /api/v1/models/import

### Description
Bulk upsert: create new models and update existing ones (matched by id). Additive, never deletes.

## POST /api/v1/models/sync

### Description
(Admin) Declarative reconcile: makes the instance match the list you send exactly, it creates, updates and deletes any model not in the payload.

## POST /api/v1/models/create

### Description
Create a single model.

## POST /api/v1/models/model/update

### Description
Update a single model.

## POST /api/v1/models/model/delete

### Description
Delete a single model.
```

--------------------------------

```APIDOC

### Description

GET

```

--------------------------------

### API Request Configuration for Reasoning Models

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/features/chat-conversations/chat-features/reasoning-models

Example JSON payload for interacting with reasoning models via the Open WebUI API, with streaming enabled for reliable parsing.

```json
{
  "model": "qwen3:32b",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Solve: What is 234 * 567?"}
  ],
  "stream": true
}
```

--------------------------------

### Llama.cpp Server API Endpoint

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/connect-a-provider/starting-with-llama-cpp

The llama-server exposes an OpenAI-compatible API. Access it locally at the specified address and port.

```bash
http://127.0.0.1:10000
```

--------------------------------

### Provider specification

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/tutorials/integrations/dev-tools/continue-dev

Defines the communication method; set to 'openai' for Open WebUI compatibility.

```yaml
provider: openai
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Connection Timeout

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/connect-a-provider/starting-with-openai-compatible

Environment variable to adjust the model list fetch timeout for slow connections or high-latency networks.

```bash
# Adjust timeout for slower connections (default is 10 seconds)
AIOHTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MODEL_LIST=5
```

--------------------------------

### Retrieve All Models via cURL

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/reference/api-endpoints

Fetches all models created or added via Open WebUI using an API key for authorization.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" http://localhost:3000/api/models
```

### Launch AUTOMATIC1111 with API support

Source: https://docs.openwebui.com/features/chat-conversations/image-generation-and-editing/automatic1111

Use these flags when starting the web UI to enable the required API endpoints and network listening.

```bash
/webui.sh --api --listen
```
